name: All Fours
description: All Fours is a classic trump trick-taking game defined by four scoring elements: High, Low, Jack, and Game. This base profile follows the Trinidad structure, with related English and North American forms listed as variations.

overview.description: All Fours is a classic trump trick-taking game defined by four scoring elements: High, Low, Jack, and Game. This base profile follows the Trinidad structure, with related English and North American forms listed as variations.

history.origins: All Fours emerged in England in the 17th century and later spread to North America and the Caribbean.
timeline: 1674: Charles Cotton records an early two-player form.
19th century: North American Old Sledge / Seven Up forms become common.
20th-21st century: Trinidad partnership form becomes the best-known living version, while Yorkshire and Lancashire forms continue in England.
history.cultural: All Fours is considered a heritage game in Trinidad and Tobago and remains a pub/league game in parts of northern England.
history.evolution: Many descendants branch from the same High-Low-Jack-Game core: Pitch, Pedro, and regional All Fours family games.

setup.players: 2-4 players; with 4, fixed partnerships across the table.
setup.dealing: Deal six cards to each player, then turn one card up for provisional trumps.

rules.objective: Reach the target score by collecting High, Low, Jack, and Game points each hand.
rules.gameplay: After six cards each and a turned trump indicator, eldest hand may stand or beg. If begging is accepted, dealer runs three more cards each and turns again until trump suit changes. In play, highest trump wins a trick; if no trump is played, highest card of the led suit wins. Players with the led suit may either follow suit or play trump, but cannot throw a non-trump card of another suit when they could follow. Score hand points in order High, Low, Jack, Game; first side to target wins the game.
keyRules: High: point to side originally holding highest trump dealt.
Low: point to side originally holding lowest trump dealt.
Jack: point if your side wins trick containing jack of trumps (hang-jack variants award extra on capture).
Game: point to side with higher trick-card value total (A=4, K=3, Q=2, J=1, 10=10).
Scores are pegged in fixed order High, Low, Jack, Game to resolve close finishes.

strategy.basic: Secure High and Low early by controlling trump suit length and timing.
strategy.intermediate: Protect or attack the Jack of trumps; that point often decides hands near the finish.
strategy.advanced: Track tens and honors in captured tricks to manage the Game point race even when trump control is split.
tips: Do not spend top trump too early if Jack is still unseen.
Game point math is ten-heavy; saving tens in winning tricks is critical.

variations.name: Trinidad All Fours
variations.description: Anticlockwise play, beg/take-one flow, target commonly 14, with hang-jack convention in many tables.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Trinidad partnership rules align with this base profile; no separate engine overrides have been modeled yet.

variations.name: West Yorkshire All Fours
variations.description: Pitch-led trump (no turn-up), scoring target 11, and regional partnership signaling/throw-in conventions.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: West Yorkshire league rules are documented in sources, but detailed engine overrides are not yet encoded for this profile.

variations.name: Lancashire All Fours
variations.description: Related to Yorkshire form, but Low can be awarded to trick winner of the low trump.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Lancashire differences are summarized in text; engine-level changes such as Low handling are not yet split into overrides.

variations.name: North American Seven Up / Old Sledge
variations.description: Clockwise forms with gift/run options, often to 7 or 10, and tie conventions for Game point.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: North American Seven Up uses the same High-Low-Jack-Game core; scoring and target variations are noted but not yet parameterized.

variations.name: 17th-Century All Fours
variations.description: Two-player historical form from Cotton with related run-card and scoring details.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Cotton’s historical rules are captured in history text; this engine does not yet branch into a dedicated 17th-century override.

scoring.description: Each hand can award up to four core points: High, Low, Jack, and Game.
scoring.winCondition: First side to 14 points in this base profile wins; other targets are variation-specific.

synthesis.shortDescription: Classic trump trick-taking game where every hand awards High, Low, Jack, and Game.
